beats.beat: In the Earlmere drying sheds, Garret teaches Elin the rule of the harvest: a glass leaf may only be cut once its central vein has turned fully silver, never before, or it will fall silent when it's needed.
Elin reaches for a borderline leaf and Garret stops her hand sharply, telling her the rule has never once failed him in all his years cutting.

Dessa Fenwick arrives at the mill shaken, carrying a dead detector bundle, and explains she nearly rode her mule straight into a hollow of bad air in the Ashfall Marches because the leaves never chimed.
Garret checks the bundle's tag against the batch number and realizes these leaves, though sold under Mabel Odell's mark, were never cut by any harvester he knows.

turn.note: Garret's line 'Nobody I know cut these' reframes a safety lesson into a mystery about forged provenance, setting up chapter 2's trip to Mabel's ledger.

trope_note: Delivers the apprentice and the rule-that-must-not-be-broken straight and clean; the thing-nobody-has-studied trope is rightly withheld for a later chapter.
fixes: Chapter runs long against its 450-word target; trim the narrator paragraph restating the rule ('The rule was older than the trade it fed...') since the dialogue just before it already demonstrates the rule in action.
Consider tightening Dessa's first speech ('Dessa Fenwick. I run Ashfall to Tollgate...') by cutting one clause, as the near-miss is already vivid without the full sentence count.
writer_note: Have Garrett push elin hand down to stop her instead of grabbing her wrist
